findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Defs.lean:321,327 (`mul_smul_comm`, `smul_mul_assoc`, both `@[simp]`); instances at Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean:323 and Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Ring.lean:32. Compare Mathlib's own `Ring.choose_smul_choose` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Binomial.lean:464) which does the same factorial-cancellation in four `rw` lines.
findings.fix: Replace both inner calcs with the single lemma (`mul_smul_comm _ _ _` and `(mul_smul_comm _ _ _).symm`); the two remaining `simp only [nsmul_eq_mul, mul_assoc]` steps at lines 145 and 191 are likewise `(smul_mul_assoc _ _ _).symm` and `smul_mul_assoc _ _ _`. Each theorem then collapses to Mathlib's own idiom, e.g. `apply nsmul_right_injective m.factorial_ne_zero; rw [← smul_mul_assoc, ← mul_smul_comm, ← Ring.descPochhammer_eq_factorial_smul_choose, ← Ring.descPochhammer_eq_factorial_smul_choose]; exact Polynomial.smeval_mul_pow_eq _ h hc n`.
findings.issue: The inner calc (lines 152-164) proves `x ^ n * (m! • C) = m! • (x ^ n * C)` in 12 lines of `nsmul_eq_mul`/`mul_assoc`/`Nat.cast_commute` juggling. That is exactly `mul_smul_comm (m.factorial) (x ^ n) C`, which is a `@[simp]` lemma and applies because `SMulCommClass ℕ A A` holds on any semiring (`AddMonoid.nat_smulCommClass`, Mathlib/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Action/Defs.lean:323). The identical problem occurs at lines 173-183 of `pow_mul_ringChoose_eq`, where the 11-line inner calc is `(mul_smul_comm _ _ _).symm`.

findings.fix: Drop `private` and give it a public name in the module's `Main results` list (e.g. `ι_mul_ι_eq_ι_mul_ι_add_zsmul_one`), since it is the reusable form of the weight relation rather than a proof-local step.
findings.issue: `mul_ι_eq_ι_mul_add_zsmul_one` is the file's one substantive algebraic step — `[h,x] = z • x` implies `ι h * ι x = ι x * (ι h + z)` in `U(L)` — but it is `private`, so downstream Chevalley normal-ordering (root strings, products of `ι x ^ n`) cannot use it without re-deriving it. Nothing public in the repo states it; `grep -rn "mul_ι\|ι_mul" TauCeti/` finds only Clifford-algebra hits.

summary: Two proofs in Semiconj.lean spend ~25 lines on nested calc blocks of Nat.cast_commute/mul_assoc that are single applications of the simp lemmas smul_mul_assoc and mul_smul_comm, and the Kostant file wraps a 14-line calc around a two-step fact that it then hides behind `private`. Fix the boilerplate and expose the reusable weight relation.
